stem:
Farai Moyo runs a transport business in Bulawayo. His financial year ends on 31 December.

| Balances at 1 January 2025 | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Motor vehicles at cost | 84,000 |
| Provision for depreciation: motor vehicles | 33,600 |

Additional information:

1. Motor vehicles are depreciated at 20% per annum on cost (straight-line method). A full year's depreciation is charged in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal.
2. On 1 July 2025 a lorry bought on 1 January 2023 for US\$26,000 was sold for US\$14,600, received by cheque.
3. On 1 September 2025 a new lorry was bought for US\$33,750, paid by cheque.
4. Motor expenses paid during 2025 were US\$4,560. This includes insurance of US\$2,280 paid on 1 April 2025 for the year ending 31 March 2026.
5. The draft net profit for 2025 was US\$41,350. It was calculated after charging the full US\$4,560 of motor expenses, but before any depreciation for 2025 and before recording the disposal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the provision for depreciation on the lorry sold, up to the date of disposal.
parts.explanation: 20% × 26,000 = 5,200 a year for 2023 and 2024 (none in 2025, the year of disposal): 2 × 5,200 = 10,400. Charging a full year for 2025 as well gives 15,600; charging half a year for 2025 gives 13,000.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 20% × 26,000 = 5,200 a year for 2023 and 2024 (none in 2025, the year of disposal): 2 × 5,200 = 10,400. Charging a full year for 2025 as well gives 15,600; charging half a year for 2025 gives 13,000.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Prepare the disposal of motor vehicle account.

points.description: Credit: Income statement, loss on disposal 1,000 (own figure)

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Disposal of motor vehicle account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 Jul 2025 | Motor vehicles | 26,000 | 1 Jul 2025 | Provision for depreciation | 10,400 |
|  |  |  | 1 Jul 2025 | Bank | 14,600 |
|  |  |  | 31 Dec 2025 | Income statement (loss) | 1,000 |
|  |  | **26,000** |  |  | **26,000** |

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the depreciation on motor vehicles for the year ended 31 December 2025.
parts.explanation: Vehicles held at 31 December 2025: 84,000 − 26,000 + 33,750 = 91,750. 20% × 91,750 = 18,350 (full year on the new lorry, none on the lorry sold). Including the lorry sold gives 23,550; leaving out the new lorry gives 11,600.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Vehicles held at 31 December 2025: 84,000 − 26,000 + 33,750 = 91,750. 20% × 91,750 = 18,350 (full year on the new lorry, none on the lorry sold). Including the lorry sold gives 23,550; leaving out the new lorry gives 11,600.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the provision for depreciation: motor vehicles account for the year ended 31 December 2025.

points.description: Debit: Balance c/d 41,550 and equal totals of 51,950

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Provision for depreciation: motor vehicles account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 Jul 2025 | Disposal | 10,400 | 1 Jan 2025 | Balance b/d | 33,600 |
| 31 Dec 2025 | Balance c/d | 41,550 | 31 Dec 2025 | Income statement | 18,350 |
|  |  | **51,950** |  |  | **51,950** |
|  |  |  | 1 Jan 2026 | Balance b/d | 41,550 |

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the motor expenses to be charged in the income statement for 2025.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the adjusted net profit for the year ended 31 December 2025.
parts.explanation: 41,350 − depreciation 18,350 − loss on disposal 1,000 + prepaid insurance 570 = 22,570. The prepayment is added back because it had been charged as an expense.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 41,350 − depreciation 18,350 − loss on disposal 1,000 + prepaid insurance 570 = 22,570. The prepayment is added back because it had been charged as an expense.

explanation: Provision on lorry sold 10,400; loss on disposal 1,000; depreciation 2025 18,350; closing provision 41,550; motor expenses 3,990; adjusted net profit 22,570. Net book value of motor vehicles at 31 December 2025: 91,750 − 41,550 = 50,200.
hints: Under this policy the lorry sold is depreciated for 2023 and 2024 only.
The prepayment reduces the expense, so it increases profit.
